attempts.label: DANDI:001968
attempts.paper_title: Early dopamine disruption in the entorhinal cortex of a knock-in model of Alzheimer’s disease
attempts.entry_title: LEC units and dopamine-fiber photometry in APP knock-in mice (Nakagawa et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's main findings could not be tested here, and those that could mostly did not hold. Cue responses and population trajectories of entorhinal neurons, histology, old-mouse behavior, and the optogenetic and L-DOPA rescues are untestable because the dandiset lacks odor times, images and those mice. The lower dopamine signal to the novel rewarded odor in APP-KI mice and the young APP-KI memory deficit were not significant, but only 10 of 27 mice have behavior and photometry rests on inferred timing. Higher firing rates in APP-KI mice did reproduce. I also tried a Gmail draft by mistake; it was denied and nothing was created.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Nakagawa et al. (2026) on dandiset 001968, which holds sorted lateral entorhinal cortex units of 27 tetrode mice (spike times only, without event times) and 41 dopamine-fiber photometry sessions of 10 mice with their trial odors and actions. It tests unit counts and firing rates of young WT and APP-KI mice, the behaviour of the photometry mice, and the LEC dopamine signals of WT and APP-KI mice. The cue responses, population trajectories, decoding, histology, optogenetics and L-DOPA behaviour cannot be tested from the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Nakagawa et al. (2026) from dandiset 001968

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's tetrode subjects can be matched to the paper's animal lists (Supplementary Table 2 and Supplementary Fig. 2), and the matched records agree on strain, sex and the young mice's principal cell counts.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Table 2; Supplementary Fig. 2a
outcomes.notes: All 27 tetrode mice of Supplementary Table 2 are in the dandiset, and it holds no other tetrode mouse. The strain label of the source file names agrees with the paper for 25 of 27; 01398 and 01431, young WT in Supplementary Table 2 and Supplementary Fig. 2a, are labelled AD. Sex agrees for 25 of 27 (00703 is F in the files and M in the table, 00789 M against F). Principal cell counts are within 10% of Supplementary Fig. 2a for 7 of 10 young mice. 00375 holds 72 against 48, 00390 151 against 130 and 01398 203 against 112. Supplementary Table 2 lists 247, 690, 703, 925 and 941 as young APP-KI and 789, 1199, 1253, 1254 and 1517 as old. Supplementary Fig. 2a lists the second five as young, and the files' birth dates make the first five 7.3 to 11.8 months old at recording and the second 1.3 to 5.8 months.
deviations: The criterion was written by the author after the survey of the files' metadata and before any analysis of the measures.
The young groups follow Supplementary Fig. 2a where it and Supplementary Table 2 disagree.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's photometry subjects can be matched to the photometry rows of Supplementary Table 2, and the matched records agree on sex and on the number of recordings.
outcomes.source: Supplementary Table 2
outcomes.notes: 10 of the 11 photometry mice of Supplementary Table 2 are in the dandiset; 00163 (DAT-Cre, one hemisphere) is missing. Sex agrees for 9 of 10; 00265 is F in the file and M in the table. The table implies 10 and 8 hemispheres, as the Fig. 4 legends state. The mice present account for 9 and 8. The files hold one trace per trial and session (11 DAT-Cre and 30 APP-KI x DAT-Cre sessions), so hemispheres cannot be identified.
deviations: The criterion was written by the author after the survey of the files' metadata and before any analysis of the measures.

outcomes.statement: In LEC layer 2/3 of young mice, 479 neurons were recorded from 5 WT mice and 846 from 5 APP-KI mice.
outcomes.source: Results, Disrupted associative memory encoding in lateral entorhinal cortex layer 2/3 neurons, paragraph 1
outcomes.quote: recorded 479 and 846 neurons from n = 5 young WT and n = 5 young APP-KI mice, respectively
outcomes.notes: Groups of Supplementary Fig. 2a (reading P). Young APP-KI 891 units (846 +- 85, within), young WT 635 (479 +- 48, outside). Principal cells (RS label, more than 100 spikes) 677 and 564 against 636 and 423; FS 212 and 71 against 210 and 56 interneurons. With 01398 and 01431 counted as APP-KI, as the files label them (reading F), 1164 and 362, both outside. The WT surplus is in 00375, 00390 and 01398 (link-unit-mice). Old WT 860 and old APP-KI 778 units (paper 671 and 618), L-DOPA 263 and saline 286 (paper 144 and 132). The 100 duplicate '_Sum' files of 00375 are not counted. No rule over sessions gives the per mouse counts of Supplementary Fig. 2a: all sessions put 7 of 10 young mice within 10%, four-letter odor sets only 6 of 10. The first four sessions of 01398, its four-letter ones, hold exactly its 112 cells (91 more in its doubled-letter sessions), and the first five of 00375 hold 49 against 48, while 00789's sessions all have doubled-letter odor sets and its 136 cells are near the paper's 125. The criterion says only when the claim is reproduced (both totals within tolerance). The outcome is partial because the claim holds in part, one of its two totals (young APP-KI) being within tolerance and the other not.
deviations: Principal cells are the RS-labelled cells with more than 100 spikes, since the files hold no waveforms to measure the peak-trough width.

outcomes.notes: Rate over the recorded span (reading a). Principal cells median 1.22 Hz in APP-KI against 0.82 in WT (677 and 564 cells), Z = -7.18, p = 6.8e-13. Interneurons 1.13 against 0.89 Hz (212 and 71), Z = -2.21, p = 0.027. The source meanFR gives p = 1.1e-12 and 0.031, and reading F of the groups p = 6.8e-16 and 0.0073. Per mouse, the principal rate is higher in APP-KI (t(8) = -4.84, p = 0.0013). The interneuron rate is higher but not significantly (t(8) = -1.60, p = 0.149), and one APP-KI mouse (00789) has a mean of 10.3 Hz. The principal peak rate is higher in APP-KI (28.7 against 27.1 Hz, p = 0.0066). The interneuron peak rate is lower in APP-KI (29.0 against 33.6 Hz, p = 0.040). Reading (b), the AB12 trial periods only, cannot be computed, as the files hold no trial times.

outcomes.statement: In correct sessions of control mice, LEC dopamine fibers respond at T1 to prelearned Odor-A, to novel Odor-1 and to novel Odor-2; with learning the Odor-2 signal disappears while the Odor-A and Odor-1 signals remain to T5.
outcomes.source: Results, Dysfunction of lateral entorhinal cortex dopamine activity, paragraph 2; Fig. 4b
outcomes.quote: At T1, dopamine was released primarily during delay periods of prelearned rewarded Odor-A (mean z -scored GCaMP signal, 1.1 ± 0.24
outcomes.notes: Mice as units (adopted, 5 WT mice), B1, 1 to 4 s window: T1 means Odor-A 1.17, Odor-1 1.66, Odor-2 0.55, all within tolerance (B2 1.11, 1.63, 0.55; 2 to 4 s also within). With 5 mice the smallest possible two-sided signed-rank p is 0.0625, so the significance part is settled by the choice of unit, not by the data, and is not tested on this unit (by rank sum Odor-2 at T1 has p = 0.117). The outcome stands because the sessions variant, where the test can be run, gives the same outcome. Sessions as units (variant), B2, 10 correct sessions, 2 to 4 s: means 1.29, 1.67, 0.55, within tolerance; at T1 all three above precue by signed-rank (p = 0.0020, 0.0039, 0.049); at T5 Odor-A significant (p = 0.0020), Odor-2 not (p = 0.13), and Odor-1 not (p = 0.084), so that part fails. By rank sum, which is not paired and compares with precue values near 0 by construction, every condition holds with sessions (Odor-1 at T5 p = 0.0025). The signed-rank test (Supplementary Table 1) is adopted as the paper's test. Under B1 with sessions the Odor-2 T1 mean is below tolerance (0.48). The means hold under both units; the tests hold in part with sessions, and with mice they are ruled out by the design.
deviations: The photometry traces are read as sampled at 1 kHz with the cue at sample 1000, so that a trial spans -1 to 5 s. The files give neither rate nor cue time. Every trial column has mean 0 and SD 1 over samples 0 to 999 and over no other span tested, as a trace z-scored to the 1 s before cue would (claims file, Shared method, Photometry, from ref. 16), and the noise peaks at 120 Hz and its harmonics under this rate. This is an assumption.

Odor codes 1 to 4 are read as Odor-A, Odor-B, Odor-1 and Odor-2, and action codes 1 to 4 as hit, miss, false alarm and correct rejection. The files give no names. The tables zscore_A to zscore_D of each file are block means of the trials of codes 1 to 4, and actions 1 and 2 occur only with codes 1 and 3.

Timepoints T1 to T5 are blocks of 10 trials of each odor starting at round(k (n - 10) / 4), the blocks the dataset's own tables hold (notebook, data check). This fits the claims file's T1, T3 and T5 and its reading T-a for T2 and T4.

The paper's units are hemispheres (10 WT, 8 APP-KI), which the files do not identify. The Fig. 4d legend's F(4,80) for 18 hemispheres and five timepoints leaves one value per hemisphere and timepoint, so a hemisphere's sessions are pooled. The mean over a mouse's sessions (5 WT and 5 APP-KI mice), the nearest pooled unit the files allow, is adopted as an assumption. Sessions as units (11 and 30), which count repeated recordings of a hemisphere as independent, are a variant. With 5 mice a two-sided signed-rank test cannot reach p < 0.05.
The trial columns are already z-scored to the precue second, so dF/F was not recomputed. They are smoothed with a Gaussian of sigma 200 ms (claims file, Shared method, Photometry).
Genotype comes from Supplementary Table 2 (link-photometry-mice); no file states it.
Session 00266_20190405 has no Odor-1/2 trial among trials 121 to 160, so under B1 it is neither a correct nor an error session.

The text names the test against the precue rank sum and Supplementary Table 1 Wilcoxon signed-rank; both were run. The signed-rank test is adopted, as the comparison is paired; the rank sum is a variant.

outcomes.statement: In APP-KI mice, Odor-1 dopamine signals emerge late, from T3, in correct sessions and are absent in error sessions (39% of sessions), while Odor-A signals stay intact.
outcomes.source: Results, Dysfunction of lateral entorhinal cortex dopamine activity, paragraph 2; Fig. 4c; Supplementary Fig. 6b
outcomes.quote: In APP-KI mice, in contrast, signals for Odor-1 emerged in a delayed manner from T3 (Fig. 4c , top), while dopamine signals for Odor-A remained intact when mice learned the association
outcomes.notes: Error sessions are 12 of 30 APP-KI sessions (40.0%) under B2, within 39 +- 3.9, and 13 (43.3%) under B1. Signed-rank, 2 to 4 s window. With mice as units (adopted, n = 5) the smallest possible two-sided signed-rank p is 0.0625, so the significance parts are settled by the choice of unit, not by the data. Odor-1 is never significant in correct sessions and Odor-A is not significant at T1 or T5, whatever the data. The outcome stands because the sessions variant, where the tests can be run, also fails. With sessions as units (variant), Odor-1 in correct sessions is significant at T1 under B2 (p = 0.016) and at T2 under B1 (p = 0.0005), so its signal does not first appear at T3; in error sessions it is significant at T4 (p = 0.021 and 0.011); Odor-A in error sessions is not significant at T1 (p = 0.42 and 0.15). In correct sessions the Odor-1 mean rises from 0.44 at T1 to 0.91, 1.09, 1.15 and 0.96 (B2), and in error sessions it stays at -0.02 to 0.32. The two denominators of the criterion coincide, as each file is one session of one mouse.

findings.statement: The unit files hold spike times only. No odor onset, trial type, lick or trial table is in any file, so no unit can be aligned to the task, and the 13 claims on cue responses, population trajectories, similarity and decoding cannot be tested.
No waveforms or spike widths are in the unit files, only an RS or FS label in each source file name, so the paper's narrow, regular and wide spiking classes cannot be formed.

The histology, the optogenetic and L-DOPA behaviour, the behaviour-only mice, the prelearning sessions and the behaviour of the tetrode mice are not in the dandiset. Photometry mouse 00163 of Supplementary Table 2 is missing.

No file states genotype, age group or treatment. Strain appears only in the unit source file names (WT, AD, NLGF), the photometry files carry none, and the L-DOPA and saline mice are both labelled NLGF. The groups can be formed only from Supplementary Table 2 and Supplementary Fig. 2a.
The unit source file names label mice 01398 and 01431 as AD; the paper lists both as young WT (Supplementary Table 2, Supplementary Fig. 2a).

Mouse 00375's units are deposited twice: 100 files named LEC_Sim1_..._Sum.mat, with genotype 'Sim1' and age P205D, repeat the spike trains of its 99 regular files, one of them twice. The earlier published version 0.260913.1518 holds one of these copies only.
sub-mouse02491/sub-mouse02491_ses-mouse02491-20250408_obj-8lnxe6.nwb holds no units table; its notes name the source file LEC_NLGF_mouse02491_250408_ABEF_RS_TT12_01.mat.

The photometry files state no sampling rate, cue time, brain region, hemisphere or odor and action names, and call the trial columns dF/F with an unknown scale, while the columns are z-scored to their first 1000 samples. The timing (1 kHz, cue at sample 1000) and the codes had to be inferred from the data and the source's own tables.

Each photometry file holds one trace per session, while Supplementary Table 2 lists bilateral recordings in 7 of the 11 mice and the paper's units are hemispheres; the files do not say which hemisphere, or whether both were averaged.

Sex in the files differs from Supplementary Table 2 for 00265 (F against M), 00703 (F against M) and 00789 (M against F). The date of birth of 00789 makes it 1.3 to 1.6 months old at recording, below the paper's young range of 3 to 6 months.

Supplementary Table 2 lists mice 247, 690, 703, 925 and 941 as young APP-KI and 789, 1199, 1253, 1254 and 1517 as old APP-KI, while Supplementary Fig. 2a lists the second five as the young APP-KI mice. The files' birth dates agree with Supplementary Fig. 2a.

The dandiset holds more units than the paper reports: 635 against 479 for young WT, 860 and 778 against 671 and 618 for old mice, 263 and 286 against 144 and 132 for the L-DOPA cohorts. Nothing marks which units the paper analysed (for example the double-counted cells it removed). An odor-set field that doubles the novel letters (ABCCDD against ABCD) is not explained. No rule over sessions or odor sets gives the per mouse cell counts of Supplementary Fig. 2a (for 01398 its first four sessions give exactly the paper's 112, of 203).
Photometry sessions hold 99 to 269 trials with novel odors from the first trials, where the paper describes about 20 A/B-only trials followed by 160 AB12 trials.

Question for the authors (Supplementary Fig. 6d). Is the 3 SD threshold for the emergence of Odor-1 dopamine signals the SD of the precue baseline or of the session's signal? Is it over the 1 to 4 s or 2 to 4 s window, and must the window mean or any sample exceed it? With the precue SD, r ranges from 0.30 to 0.73 across these choices; with the session's SD almost no session reaches the threshold.

disagreements.reason: Under reading P, young WT has 635 units against 479 +- 48, so it fails; APP-KI has 891 against 846 +- 85, so it passes. Under reading F both fail. The criterion needs both. Problem 9: the notebook does not explain the surplus young WT units (for example 01398, 203 principal cells against 112), nor the ABCCDD-type sessions.

Sessions as units, Odor-1 exceeds A (p = 0.0013) and B (p = 0.0008). Mice as units, A against 1 p = 0.0031, B against 1 p = 0.055. Neither proxy is the paper's hemisphere unit. Problem 1: the photometry unit of analysis is not the paper's. The paper uses hemispheres, which the files do not identify. The notebook uses sessions or mice instead and prefers sessions. Sessions count each recording more than once, giving df 195 against the paper's 80 and 116 against 28. The stated reason for preferring sessions is partly that it lets the test reach significance. Problem 6: the near-zero precue contrast is forced by the per-trial z-scoring, so it does not check where the cue is. Problem 8: two_way uses type II sums of squares; MATLAB's anovan defaults to type III.

B1, both means within tolerance, but p = 0.25. B2, p = 0.046, but WT is 90.0, outside 77.5 +- 6.1. Problem 3: tested on 10 of 27 mice, so a failed test is weak evidence. Problem 5: session 00266_20190405, whose B1 performance is undefined, is counted as an error session; excluded, WT B1 is 83.3% and p = 0.067.

entries.name: nakagawa-2026
entries.title: LEC units and dopamine-fiber photometry in APP knock-in mice (Nakagawa et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Nakagawa et al. (2026) on dandiset 001968, which holds sorted lateral entorhinal cortex units of 27 tetrode mice (spike times only, without event times) and 41 dopamine-fiber photometry sessions of 10 mice with their trial odors and actions. It tests unit counts and firing rates of young WT and APP-KI mice, the behaviour of the photometry mice, and the LEC dopamine signals of WT and APP-KI mice. The cue responses, population trajectories, decoding, histology, optogenetics and L-DOPA behaviour cannot be tested from the dandiset.
